notice: Synthetic, curated demonstration guidance. Not a real carrier procedure or policy.

documents.title: General eSIM activation checklist
documents.content: The digital SIM (eSIM) is the mobile line profile installed on a compatible device. Confirm the device supports eSIM and is connected to reliable Wi-Fi. Open the device's cellular settings and follow the carrier activation flow or scan the current, unused activation QR code. Keep the activation screen open until the digital SIM profile is installed, then select the new line for mobile data and restart the device once. Do not scan a QR code that was issued to another customer or has already been used.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if the activation profile is missing from the account, the QR code is expired or already consumed, or activation still fails after one clean retry.

documents.title: E4037 error during eSIM activation
documents.content: If E4037 appears while activating a digital SIM (eSIM), record the exact error and time, then confirm the device supports eSIM and has a working Wi-Fi connection. Check that the intended line is eligible for eSIM and that its activation profile has not already been installed or used. Restart the device once and retry the current activation flow only once; do not repeatedly scan the same code. If E4037 returns, stop retries and ask an authorized support agent to verify line provisioning and issue a fresh profile when appropriate.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate immediately after E4037 repeats once, the line is absent or suspended in account records, or the activation code appears used or issued to a different line.

documents.title: eSIM profile download is stuck or fails
documents.content: Keep the device on stable Wi-Fi while the digital SIM (eSIM) profile downloads, and disable any VPN temporarily if permitted by the customer's organization. Check that automatic date and time are enabled and that the device has free storage. Restart once, then resume activation from the carrier app or device settings without requesting multiple profiles. Avoid deleting an installed profile until support confirms that it can be reissued.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if the profile remains pending after one retry or if the device shows a profile installed but the line is not provisioned.

documents.title: New SIM registration remains pending
documents.content: Confirm that the SIM is inserted correctly or that the eSIM profile is enabled, then restart the device in an area with known coverage. Allow a short registration interval and check whether the device displays the expected network name. Verify that the line is active in the customer's account rather than relying on the handset status alone.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if registration remains pending after a restart or the account shows the line as inactive, restricted, or assigned to another SIM.

documents.title: SIM registration rejected
documents.content: Reseat a physical SIM with the device powered off, or confirm the correct eSIM line is enabled. Check for a visible error message and try one restart. Do not change network selection repeatedly or share the full SIM identifier in an unsecured channel. An authorized agent should verify the line-to-SIM assignment and activation state.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate when the rejection persists or the SIM assignment does not match the verified account record.

documents.title: 5G option is not available
documents.content: Check that the handset model and software support the local 5G bands and that the customer's plan includes 5G access. In mobile network settings, enable the 5G preferred mode if the device offers it. Test outdoors or near a window because building materials can limit coverage. A 4G connection can be expected where 5G coverage is unavailable.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if coverage maps and device compatibility indicate service should be available but the line remains provisioned for a lower network tier.

documents.title: 5G connection repeatedly drops
documents.content: Check whether the issue occurs in one location or across several areas. Update device software, restart once, and temporarily select automatic network mode rather than forcing 5G where signal is weak. Compare service on 4G to determine whether the symptom is limited to 5G coverage. Preserve the time and approximate location of repeated drops for investigation.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if the drops persist across locations after software and network-mode checks, or if multiple users report the same local failure.

documents.title: Mobile data is enabled but internet does not work
documents.content: Confirm mobile data is enabled for the intended SIM and that airplane mode is off. Check the account for an active data allowance and any usage restriction. Toggle airplane mode once, wait for registration, then restart if needed. Test one trusted website with Wi-Fi turned off to distinguish mobile data from a Wi-Fi connection problem.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if data remains unavailable in a covered area with an active allowance after one network refresh and restart.

documents.title: Mobile data access point settings
documents.content: First use the device's automatic network settings or the carrier's verified configuration profile. Do not guess access point names or proxy values because incorrect settings can interrupt service or route traffic unexpectedly. If settings were changed, record them and restore the device's default or carrier-provided profile, then restart mobile data.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate when the carrier profile is unavailable or verified settings still fail across more than one location.

documents.title: Mobile data is unusually slow
documents.content: Repeat a basic speed check in a second location and note whether the device is on 4G or 5G. Pause large downloads and close applications that are actively transferring data. Check current allowance and any plan limits; do not use one speed result as proof of a network fault. Restart once and compare service at a different time.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if consistently poor service is reproduced in multiple locations with available allowance and compatible device settings.

documents.title: Phone shows no service
documents.content: Check for a local outage and move to an open area with known coverage. Confirm the SIM is enabled and the line is active, then toggle airplane mode once and restart the handset. If available, compare with another compatible device or SIM only with the account holder's permission. Do not factory-reset the device as an initial troubleshooting step.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate promptly if the line cannot register in multiple covered locations or the user needs service for an urgent safety or accessibility need.

documents.title: Mobile network disconnects intermittently
documents.content: Record the times and places where the connection drops and whether calls, messages, data, or all services are affected. Restart once, install pending device updates, and leave network selection on automatic. Compare another location to separate local coverage from a device or line issue. Avoid repeated network resets that erase useful configuration.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if the problem repeats across locations or affects several services after basic checks.

documents.title: Check and respond to a network outage
documents.content: Check the provider's official service-status channel using Wi-Fi or another connection. Note the affected area and the reported restoration update without promising an estimated time beyond the published notice. Keep the handset on automatic network selection and retry only after the status changes. A local outage should not be treated as a handset fault.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if the official status is clear but service remains unavailable after restoration, or if no status exists for a widespread verified incident.

documents.title: Weak signal in one location
documents.content: Move near a window or outdoors and compare signal in another nearby location. Remove a thick case temporarily if it may obstruct the antenna, and confirm the device supports the local network bands. Check for construction, terrain, or indoor coverage limitations. Do not promise coverage indoors based only on an outdoor map.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate persistent loss in a previously served area or a change affecting multiple nearby subscribers.

documents.title: Enable international roaming safely
documents.content: Before travel, verify that the account and plan permit roaming in the destination. Review the applicable rates and any data pass in the official account channel. Enable data roaming only when needed and consider disabling background data or using trusted Wi-Fi. Save the support contact method that works outside the home network.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if the destination is unsupported, rates are unclear, or the account shows roaming blocked despite verified eligibility.

documents.title: No mobile service while roaming
documents.content: Confirm international roaming is enabled on the account and in device settings. Restart once, keep network selection automatic, and allow the handset a few minutes to register. If automatic registration fails, choose a listed partner network only when the provider's travel guidance supports it, then return to automatic selection after testing.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate when the account is eligible but cannot register on supported partner networks, especially if the customer has no alternate communication method.

documents.title: Unexpected international roaming charges
documents.content: Review the itemized usage dates, destination network, and service type in the account. Compare usage with the travel dates and any purchased pass; delayed network records can post after travel. Turn off data roaming and background data while the charge is reviewed. Do not promise a credit before the billing review is complete.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate disputed charges with dates and itemized records to the authorized billing team; escalate urgently if suspected account compromise or ongoing unrecognized usage is present.

documents.title: Prepaid recharge failed
documents.content: Check the recharge confirmation and account balance before attempting another payment. Confirm the phone number and selected plan are correct, then refresh the account view after a short wait. If no debit occurred and no recharge is pending, retry once using the official payment channel. Keep the receipt or transaction reference.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if payment was taken, the transaction remains pending beyond the displayed processing window, or repeated attempts were charged.

documents.title: Recharge payment is pending
documents.content: Do not submit another recharge while the first transaction is pending. Save the transaction reference and check the official account history after the payment provider's stated processing window. Confirm whether the balance or plan validity changed. A pending card authorization may later reverse, so distinguish an authorization from a settled debit.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate a settled debit without a credited recharge after the published processing window, or any second debit for the same transaction.

documents.title: Payment deducted but recharge not credited
documents.content: Check whether the payment is settled, pending, or reversed and capture its reference, amount, and time. Verify that the recharge was intended for the correct line and inspect account history after the stated processing window. Do not ask the customer to send full card details, passwords, or one-time codes. Avoid retrying while the original debit is unresolved.
documents.escalation_conditions: Route to payment reconciliation if a settled debit has no matching recharge after the processing window; report suspected unauthorized payment through the account-security path.

documents.title: Possible duplicate payment
documents.content: Compare each transaction's date, amount, merchant descriptor, and status before concluding that a duplicate settled. One entry may be a temporary authorization that will disappear. Do not initiate repeated refunds or another payment while the records are being checked. Share only masked references through approved support channels.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate two settled matching debits or an unrecognized debit to the authorized payment team; advise account-security review when the customer did not authorize either transaction.

documents.title: Unexpected amount on a monthly bill
documents.content: Compare the current bill with the prior cycle and identify the changed line item, date range, tax, plan fee, add-on, or one-time charge. Check whether a plan change or discount expiry occurred during the cycle. Explain only charges visible in the account record and submit a billing review for unexplained items. Keep the disputed amount and reference documented.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate an unexplained recurring charge, a charge inconsistent with the account agreement, or a dispute nearing its response deadline.

documents.title: Customer account is locked
documents.content: Use the official account recovery flow and follow the displayed wait period rather than repeating failed attempts. Confirm access to the registered recovery method without requesting the password or one-time code. If the customer no longer controls that method, use the provider's verified identity-recovery procedure through an authorized agent.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if recovery methods were changed without authorization, repeated lockouts continue, or the customer cannot complete the approved identity checks.

documents.title: Password reset message does not arrive
documents.content: Verify that the customer entered the account's registered email address and check spam, blocked senders, and mailbox capacity. Wait for the normal delivery interval before requesting one new reset message; use only the latest link. Never ask the customer to share the link, password, or verification code. If the registered address is inaccessible, use the verified recovery process.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if no reset message arrives after one resend or the registered contact information appears to have changed without authorization.

documents.title: Suspected SIM swap or sudden loss of service
documents.content: Treat unexplained loss of mobile service together with unexpected account changes as a possible SIM-swap incident. Direct the customer to contact the provider through a verified alternate channel and request account protection and line review. Secure the associated email and financial accounts from a trusted device. Do not send reset codes to the affected number or disclose account details until identity is verified.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate immediately to the designated account-security team when a SIM change was not authorized or the customer reports financial or identity misuse.

documents.title: Suspected customer account compromise
documents.content: Use a trusted device and verified contact route to report the concern. Follow the provider's identity-verification and account-lock procedure; do not ask for passwords, payment card numbers, or one-time codes in chat. Recommend changing credentials on the account and its recovery email, and reviewing recent line, SIM, and payment changes. Preserve timestamps and affected account actions for the security case.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate immediately for unauthorized SIM, contact, password, or payment changes, or any evidence of ongoing access.

documents.title: Check handset network compatibility
documents.content: Confirm the exact handset model and regional variant, not only the retail family name. Compare its supported bands and SIM capabilities with the service being activated. Install current operating-system updates and confirm the handset is not restricted by a separate device lock. Compatibility information should come from verified manufacturer or provider references.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate when published compatibility references conflict or the account reports an unsupported-device error despite a matching model variant.

documents.title: Verify eSIM device compatibility
documents.content: Check the manufacturer's specification for the exact regional model and confirm eSIM support for that variant. Confirm the device is not carrier-locked in a way that prevents the intended profile and that the operating system is current. Some devices support eSIM hardware but not every transfer or dual-SIM configuration. Do not promise compatibility based solely on the product name.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if the exact model variant is unclear or a supported device is rejected by the activation system.

documents.title: Device may be locked to another provider
documents.content: Check the device's official SIM status or ask the original seller for unlock eligibility. A network lock is different from a SIM activation error and cannot be cleared by changing APN settings. Use the original provider's authorized unlock process and avoid unofficial unlock utilities that request payment or device credentials.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate to the device seller or original provider if the lock status cannot be verified or the authorized unlock request is rejected.

documents.title: Outgoing calls fail on a registered mobile line
documents.content: Confirm the line is active, the device has signal, and the number is dialed in the expected format. Restart once and test a second destination to determine whether only one number is affected. Check whether voice service is enabled for the plan and whether a device setting is restricting calls. Avoid repeatedly retrying emergency calls through a failing line; use an available alternate emergency method.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate immediately if all calls fail across a covered area or the customer cannot place an urgent safety call.

documents.title: SMS or verification messages are delayed
documents.content: Check signal, message storage, blocked senders, and whether the line is currently registered. Ask the sender to confirm the destination number and wait briefly before requesting a single new verification message. Short-code delivery can be restricted by roaming, account settings, or the sending service. Do not ask the customer to disclose the code itself.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if ordinary SMS also fails, the line recently changed SIM, or only a specific sender's messages remain undelivered after sender-side checks.

documents.title: Number transfer is taking longer than expected
documents.content: Check the transfer status and any stated completion window through the official account channel. Confirm that the current provider account details and transfer authorization match exactly; do not cancel the old service while the transfer is pending. Keep the old SIM available until the new line registers and test calls and messages after completion.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if the published transfer window has passed, the request is rejected for unclear information, or both services are unavailable after a status change.

documents.title: Data allowance appears exhausted
documents.content: Review the account's current-cycle data usage and plan limit; device counters may cover a different period. Identify whether the plan reduces speed, blocks data, or charges additional usage, using the account's published terms. Connect to trusted Wi-Fi for large downloads and avoid changing the plan until the account holder understands any new charge.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if account usage is inconsistent with itemized records or a restriction remains after the cycle or plan status changes.

documents.title: Service is restricted after an account payment issue
documents.content: Check the account status and payment history before asking the customer to pay again. Distinguish a pending payment from a settled payment and use the official payment channel. If payment is confirmed but service remains restricted, allow the published update interval and request a service-status refresh. Do not promise immediate restoration unless the account record confirms it.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate a settled payment with continued restriction beyond the stated update interval or any case where duplicate payment may result.

documents.title: Automatic payment did not process
documents.content: Check the payment status and account notice before initiating a manual payment. Confirm whether the payment method is expired or needs issuer verification, without collecting full card details in support chat. If the customer chooses another method, use the official secure payment page and save the receipt. Check service status after the payment is confirmed.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if the account shows a settled debit but an unpaid balance, or if multiple automatic attempts were made.

documents.title: Check the status of an approved payment reversal
documents.content: Confirm that a reversal or refund was actually approved and record its reference and date. Explain that posting time depends on the payment method and financial institution; do not guarantee a date not shown in the account record. Ask the customer to compare the original transaction with any pending credit and avoid submitting a duplicate refund request while it is processing.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate when the published posting interval has passed or the account has no record of a refund the customer was told was approved.

documents.title: Choose the correct line for dual-SIM mobile data
documents.content: In cellular settings, confirm both the intended eSIM and the physical SIM are enabled. Select the intended line for mobile data and verify that data switching behavior is understood before testing. If the device has multiple active lines, place a test call on each line and check which line is using data. Avoid deleting either profile during diagnosis.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if the intended line is not selectable or the account shows a profile assignment inconsistent with the device.

documents.title: Wi-Fi calling is unavailable
documents.content: Confirm the handset and plan support Wi-Fi calling and that the feature is enabled in device settings. Connect to a stable private Wi-Fi network and verify that emergency address or service information required by the device is complete. Restart the handset after changing the setting. Public or restricted Wi-Fi networks may block the connection.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if the feature is enabled on a compatible line but fails across more than one stable Wi-Fi network.

documents.title: General conditions for support escalation
documents.content: Escalate instead of repeating basic steps when a verified account or provisioning issue is present, a failure persists across locations or devices, a payment is settled but service or credit is missing, or the customer reports unauthorized account activity. Record observed symptoms, timestamps, safe troubleshooting already completed, and the relevant account reference. Do not represent an unverified cause as confirmed.
documents.escalation_conditions: Use specialist escalation for account security, repeated activation identifiers, disputed settled payments, widespread outage, or an unresolved safety/accessibility impact.

documents.title: Escalate a suspected widespread service outage
documents.content: Record the affected service, approximate area, first observed time, and whether other users report the same symptom. Check the official incident channel before describing an outage as confirmed. Preserve an alternate contact route for customers without service. Avoid repeatedly asking customers to reset devices during a verified area incident.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate through the incident process when multiple independent reports indicate a shared failure or a verified outage has no current status update.

documents.title: Customer reports a suspicious telecom message
documents.content: Tell the customer not to open links, install apps, or reply with credentials or verification codes. They should access the account by typing the known official address or using the installed official app, then review recent changes. Preserve the sender and message details through an approved reporting channel, taking care not to forward active malicious links broadly.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate immediately if the customer entered a password or code, installed an unexpected app, or sees an unauthorized account or SIM change.

documents.title: Roaming usage appears after a delay
documents.content: Explain that roaming records can arrive after the service was used, so the bill posting date may differ from the travel date. Compare itemized usage dates and destination details with the travel itinerary and any roaming pass. Pause roaming data while a disputed amount is reviewed. Treat late-posted usage and duplicate billing as separate issues until the records are reconciled.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate if itemized usage has no matching travel or line activity, or the same event appears as duplicate settled charges.

documents.title: Replace a damaged or lost SIM
documents.content: Verify the account holder through the approved process and confirm which line needs replacement. Use only the official SIM replacement or eSIM reissue workflow. If the SIM was lost or stolen, request immediate line protection before issuing a replacement. Test registration, calls, and data after replacement and keep the old SIM disabled.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate a lost SIM with unexplained account activity as a security case; escalate replacement failures when the line-to-SIM assignment cannot be confirmed.

documents.title: When to use a device network settings reset
documents.content: Try a normal restart and verify line selection before resetting network settings. A network reset may remove saved Wi-Fi networks, VPN settings, and paired connections, so explain the effect and obtain consent first. Record any carrier profile details needed to restore connectivity. Do not factory-reset the device as a routine network troubleshooting step.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate before a reset when the device is managed by an employer or the customer cannot restore required network credentials.

documents.title: Recharge is confirmed but balance has not refreshed
documents.content: Check the receipt and transaction state in the official account history. Sign out and back in or refresh the balance view once, then wait for the displayed update interval. Confirm whether the plan or balance was credited to a different line. Do not ask the customer to repeat the transaction while the confirmed recharge is reconciling.
documents.escalation_conditions: Escalate a confirmed transaction that remains uncredited beyond the published update interval or appears on the wrong line.
